simple.meaning: שָׁחִיס (shâchîyç) is a Hebrew word meaning “after-growth.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: שָׁחִיס (H7823) appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at 2 Kings 19:29, with occurrences in 2 Kings, Isaiah.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to שָׁחִיס (H7823) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in שָׁחִיס (H7823) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: שָׁחִיס (shâchîyç) / H7823 is traced through 2 Kings 19:29, Isaiah 37:30 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H7823. shachis or sachish סָחִישׁ noun [masculine] grain that shoots up of itself in 2nd year (√ unknown); — || סָפִיחַ , 2Kin 19:29 (= שָׁחִיס || Isa 37:30 ); on use of this for food, compare Strabo xi. 4, 3 (of Albanians).
definitions.rootNote: or סָחִישׁ ; from an unused root apparently meaning to sprout ;

occurrences.englishText: “This will be the sign to you: This year, you will eat that which grows of itself, and in the second year that which springs from that; and in the third year sow, and reap, and plant vineyards, and eat its fruit.

“ ‘This shall be the sign to you. You will eat this year that which grows of itself, and in the second year that which springs from it; and in the third year sow and reap and plant vineyards, and eat their fruit.
